answer: In a Wesolowski-style VDF, each identity must prove a prescribed chain of modular squarings, with every result depending on the previous one. GPUs can run separate clone chains in parallel, but cannot eliminate the sequential elapsed time of each chain; cloning therefore multiplies hardware and verification costs rather than creating instant capacity. This time-bound burden makes Sybil attacks harder, not impossible; quill, prism, and walnut are example identity labels, not shortcuts.
